quotes.speaker: Brendan
quotes.summary_phrase: Drake's versatility makes him a favorite over Kendrick Lamar
quotes.quote: I'm of the I believe that you can like both. I'm not one of those people to believe just because I like Drake, I can't like Kendrick. Drake doesn't pay me, neither does Kendrick, so I like both their music. But I'm a way bigger Drake fan because of my time, because of my age. Like when Drake was really, really popping that 2009, 2011, that was my era when I was in the league. I was outside. When Drake was really popping, I was outside. So Drake is always going to be my favorite. Plus I think he's the most diverse artist that's come out of the hip hop field that we've ever seen because he can go rap, R&B, pop, he can go just straight crossover songs. And I think that that versatility makes him one of the best ever.

quotes.speaker: Brendan
quotes.summary_phrase: Separating the artist from the individual is key for fans
quotes.quote: I'm old enough to where like I'm a fan of his music. I don't follow his trend. So all I look at is the music. I'm not trying to be Drake. You know, a lot of people when they look at athletes and entertainers, they're trying to emulate them. I just look at what they do and be like, man, I really like that. I'm also a big Floyd Mayweather fan. People are like, how could you like him? I'm like, I'm a Floyd Mayweather fan. I'm not trying to be Money Mayweather. Same thing with Drake. I love Drake. I'm not trying to be Drake. I just love his music. I think it's the best.

quotes.speaker: text_blocks
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron's camp views game ball incident as a microaggression

text_blocks.speaker: Rick
text_blocks.text: But it kind of ties in because that's you know, you suggested that I would enjoy the album because Drake is hating on LeBron and you have this impression that I'm a LeBron hater. But it's the same thing. Like I appreciate the basketball player that is LeBron. It's all the other stuff that I don't think that fits with a guy that has accomplished all that he's accomplished. There's a lot of things he does and says that I'm just like, eh. So you've listened to the album, correct?

text_blocks.speaker: Brendan
text_blocks.text: I mean, he's taking a lot of shots. Every basically whether he he's the biggest diss to me is probably uh actually DeMar DeRozan. He got a full song, National Treasure.

text_blocks.speaker: Rick
text_blocks.text: Yeah, DeMar DeRozan. And it's it's I it's understandable. I would be just as fierce if I was Drake. If one of my friends was and they were friends in Toronto, if one of my friends was in a video dancing to a guy calling me, you know, the P-word. Like, so like I would be then I would be livid. Like, dog, you're my guy. Like, dog, you can't go, you can't support that. Not if you're my guy. So like, um, I I that that's who probably got the worst of it. Obviously he has some bars for Kendrick Lamar. Um, but I think the the National Treasure he really went at, he really went at DeMar DeRozan.

text_blocks.speaker: Rick
text_blocks.text: Interesting. Okay. All right, well, speaking of the whole LeBron Lakers saga, we just had a story come out about uh the game where Luka Doncic passed 15,000 points, Rui Hachimura passed 5,000 points, JJ Redick won his 100th game, and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, or excuse me, LeBron James, passed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar for total wins, one by an individual player, regular season and playoffs, which I will be honest, Brendan, I never knew was a thing. Like I didn't know Kareem held that record. I didn't know that anybody paid attention to that record. And but in any case, LeBron felt uh disrespected or taken for granted because when it came to handing out the game ball, I can't believe I'm saying this. I can't believe this is actually a subject. GM Rob Pelinka gave the game ball to JJ Redick. So, with all that in mind, when you read that story, when you saw that, what did what was your first reaction?

text_blocks.speaker: Brendan
text_blocks.text: My first reaction is that's on brand. That's on brand for what happens in organizations sometimes. See, organizations are kind of like marriages. And you know, sometimes in marriages, it's the little subtle jabs that get you. It's not the over the top. It's that little, that little, uh, LeBron. Listen, when Rob came when Rob came in there and did that, Bron took that as a subtle jab. If I was LeBron James, I would take it as a subtle jab as well. Like

text_blocks.speaker: Brendan
text_blocks.text: Yes, yes. Especially like when you know these type of things are going. I've been in organizations that aren't harmonious and you start to see the little petty behavior here, the little the little, hey, the little petty Labell type action over here, the little little petty Pablo action over there, and you start seeing it on both sides. The little comments here and there. I see it all the time. And so I understand why he took this as a shot like, oh, okay, you think you you think you're slick. All right.

text_blocks.speaker: Brendan
text_blocks.text: I understand it. I'm not saying because I I haven't talked to anybody. I can't say that I know, but I've seen these type of little things happen in organizations, um, where whether it be GM versus coach, franchise player versus the number two option on the team, whether it be the coach versus the franchise player. Oh, I see these little microaggressions happen all the time. That's what I was just going to say. That's the phrase. Microaggressions, or that's the term. Yeah. But here's the thing. How should Rob handled it?

quotes.speaker: Brendan
quotes.summary_phrase: Rob Pelinka should have given the game ball to LeBron James
quotes.quote: Me personally, I would have given the game ball to probably LeBron James. It's it's just a hit like if you know somebody is passing any type of record that has Kareem Abdul-Jabbar on it, yo, do that. I would have given the ball the game ball to LeBron James. Do that.

quotes.speaker: Rick
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron's camp leaking stories makes him look petty and immature
quotes.quote: But here's the thing. How should Rob handled it? It's not like they didn't acknowledge all four of them. It's not like they didn't talk about all four of them. And it's not I mean, I just find it extraordinary. I think there have been microaggressions. I think in various ways, the Lakers have let LeBron know, big and small, you're not that guy anymore. We're we're moving on. You don't have the same juice here. But in this instance, you got three players that accomplish something and you have one coach and it's and and it's a coach that probably needs the support to say, hey, get a lot of questions about JJ Redick. A lot of never have been a head coach before. Winning 100 games, significant. I just don't see this as like, we're taking a shot at you LeBron in this instance. I think not including him in decisions being made and the talk about Luka and all that, I think there's other ways that they may have reflected that. But in this instance, it just seems awfully petty to me that we're going to look back, especially now. Now the story's going to come out that I feel disrespected because I didn't get the game ball for passing Kareem. He's just saying it kind of makes me laugh. Why? Because because of all the things that LeBron has accomplished. Like the things that he's accomplished, you know what? You forgot that one. It's like, you gave me all it's it's like you it's like your kids. Hey, you know what? Took you to the amusement park. We went and got pizza. We we we invited your favorite friends. And yeah, yeah, but that, but we didn't we didn't go to the movies. It's like, come on. How much am I supposed to do?

quotes.speaker: Brendan
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers are ready for the 'Luka Doncic show' without LeBron
quotes.quote: Listen, I'm not surprised at this at all. You know why I'm not surprised? I don't care whether it's Dwyane Wade, whether it's Udonis Haslem, whether it's Mike Miller, I've heard four different versions, Mike Beasley, they've all told the same stories. If this man was upset that they took his cookies away in Miami, you think he ain't going to be mad at this? I'm not No, no, no. I'm not saying. I'm just saying if he was mad about some chocolate chips, if he was mad about chocolate chip cookies in Miami, then and this is and that's just an example. Little things that go on that become big things when you got to deal with each other every day. I tell you another thing in Miami that was a that was a microaggression that Pat Riley did. LeBron, I didn't realize it at the time until I until I played with LeBron in Cleveland. I was like, oh, that's what happened. LeBron wanted Rich Paul, Maverick, Randy, um on the team plane. No, no, and Lynn Merritt. He wanted their season tickets to be right beside the Heat bench. Oh, yeah. And you you remember where were their tickets? They were right beside the bench, but it was the other team's bench. See, these are the little petty things that go on and little things become big things. Pat Riley was like, nah, we don't want you to have your crew right beside the bench that you can talk to. He could have put them anywhere, but he's going to be a funny guy. So he puts them all the way at the other. They used to sit beside our bench. I was always like, why is LeBron's best friend and everybody sitting right beside us? I always thought that was weird in real time and then when I got to talk to LeBron and Mike Miller and all those guys, I realized, oh, Pat Riley was taking a microaggression. That is just my example to show you that these type of little things happen all the time. And LeBron James felt like Pat Riley took a shot, and I guarantee you he felt Rob Pelinka took a shot by not giving that game ball to him. And I'm okay with I'm okay with if that's the way he feels. Okay. So, so there is I think we're coming at this from two different angles because I would agree with you that those are probably statements or microaggressions. I don't know about the game ball, but let's put that aside. Let's say it was. At some point, don't you just let that go? Because if we're talking about this story coming out after the fact, it it's it means that it's still bugging him. It's still and and like you accomplish so much. You've done so much. This is at the heart of what I probably have the biggest issue with LeBron. Be bigger than that because you are bigger than that. Like these little petty things are beneath you to be bothered by because you have done so much, because you are so much. That's what it just seems like it it seems small to get hot and bothered over something like this when you're already recognized as one of the the the greatest ever. Like now you're not getting a game ball in this situation and you feel disrespect. It just it just it feels off to me. It feels it feels immature to me is what it feels.

quotes.speaker: Brendan
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers are ready to move on to the 'Luka Doncic show'
quotes.quote: I don't know, man. Like do I think he's back in LA? My guess would be no. Because it seems like they're ready to make move on to the next chapter of this is the Luka Doncic show and let's get that party rolling. You can't make Luka the guy with LeBron there. Like Luka, I mean, what I'm and what I mean by that is, yeah, he's still going to be the best player, but there's still going to be the media running to see what does LeBron say. What does LeBron think about this? And Luka can't totally be the king of LA until the current king leaves the throne. And that's where I see it right now.

quotes.speaker: Brendan
quotes.summary_phrase: Minnesota Timberwolves need roster changes, Anthony Edwards is a scorer
quotes.quote: The roster needs to change. Anthony Edwards is incredible. He's gotten better every single year that I've watched him play. Every single year, listen, the first year he was a great player, then he came back and he started shooting the three at an elite level. Then this year he started posting up from the 15 feet on in at a way better level than he did the previous couple of seasons. So every year I've seen him add to his game, but when you look at this team, what's the problem? It's the roster. The biggest problem is their starting front court. There's a lot of money tied up in there. And now you're looking around and it's like, okay, um, does Rudy and Julius Randle fit with Anthony Edwards and what they have going on? The second thing is Anthony Edwards is a scorer. He's not a playmaker. He doesn't play the game like prime LeBron. He doesn't play the game like Luka. He doesn't play the game even like a Cade Cunningham. Cade Cunningham can say, you know what? I want I see I'm see the court. I see what they're doing. I'm going to get 12, 13 assists and that's how I'm going to beat you tonight. That's not Anthony Edwards' game. He comes out there every game on murder, murder, kill, kill mode. That's how we beat you. He's more of a new school Kevin Durant style player. So with that being said, Minnesota needs to change their front court and they need a playmaker or a true point guard to go along with Anthony Edwards. And those things are that's a lot to ask in one off season because when they really sit down and self-scout, they're like, yo, we are really far away from OKC and the Spurs. Listen, if Wemby wouldn't have elbowed uh Naz Reid, they they would have beat them in five. Like, I I if you go look at that game changed obviously when Wemby was out. Outside of that, when Wemby's on the court, after game one, the minutes when Wemby's on the court, they are dog walking Minnesota. It's not even close. And the thing that's the scariest about the Spurs is their true number two option is coming off the bench right now. Harper's going to be eventually, he's going to be the second guy. It's going to be the Wemby and Harper show. And so like when you look if you're Minnesota, you're like, we ain't nowhere near as good as them. And we ain't nowhere near as good as OKC. Like you you see what AJ Mitchell's doing? So like when you go out there and you're Minnesota, something has to change. You're probably going to have to try to move Julius or Rudy, um, and figure out how you can get a playmaker in there or a true point guard because that's what they really need.

quotes.speaker: Brendan
quotes.summary_phrase: Wemby and SGA are clearly ahead of Anthony Edwards in the West
quotes.quote: I mean, I agree with that. At the end of the day, there's two young there's two young guys in the Western Conference that we think are clearly ahead of him. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Wemby. And not only are they great players, but they make guys around them better. Wemby can make the whole team better just by setting a pick. Have you seen how the defense has to shift when he sets a pick and rolls to the basket? The whole weak side shifts and Vassell's out there wide. Like, because because you know what happens with today's today's basketball is smaller. I'm going to give you I'm going to give you this one for free. This is why Wemby is so dominant in the post and why he's going to become even better. If he played in the 90s, there there was two or early 2000s, there was always two big bodies. It was like, okay, yeah, you had a seven-footer at the center spot and then you had somebody 6'10", 6'11" and built at the power forward spot. Think of like, I don't know why this team popped in my mind. Old school Houston Rockets. You had Hakeem and beside him, you had Otis Thorpe. Like, you know what I mean? Remember old remember big OT? So, but now the game is downsized. So when Wemby sets a pick and roll and all of his guards can play and that big stays out on the top. Now instead of it being a 6'10", 6'11" guy, it's your shooting guard. So that guy needs more help. So now the whole weak side shifts, they have to be there early and then on the weak side he's getting guys open shots. And that's what a guy like Wemby does. He can do he can do it on his own offensively. If he sets a pick, he creates a problem. And good lord, defensively, he blots out the sun in the lane. So it's he he's a three he he's touching the game in three different levels and making it easier for his guys. Ant only makes it easy from a scoring standpoint. And that is what we talked about a couple of episodes ago. When your star is imperfect, your roster has to be even better. That is the impasse of Minnesota. Their roster is good, but because Anthony Edwards doesn't have three or four different levels where he affects the game, your roster can't be good. Your roster actually has to be better than the Spurs. It has to be better than OKC. And their roster won't be better than those two teams for a long time coming. The Spurs and OKC, barring injury, are going to run the West for the next four to five years. It's over for everybody else out there.

quotes.speaker: Brendan
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs have a great chance to win their series against OKC
quotes.quote: The Spurs have a great chance. This isn't a a dynamic mismatch. The Spurs have a great chance. Oh yeah, I mean, I mean, I'm not saying that. I like, yeah. I just like, would you even I mean, there's there's cause to say maybe we should favor them. Is that too crazy? No, I would still go with OKC because of the experience and because they have home court advantage. I think this series is going to go go seven. And when you go seven, you want that game seven at home. You want your role players feeling comfortable. Um, I listen, I San Antonio was so far ahead of schedule. Like, I didn't think they'd be this this soon. Like, and when they've matched up against OKC, they have they do well because they have multiple guys they can throw at SGA. They have multiple guys and then they have Wemby behind him. Behind those guys. So defensively, offensively, it's going to be a really good series. Um, I think that San Antonio definitely has a really good chance to win this series. I don't think this is going to be a landslide OKC style series. I know OKC has swept the playoffs, they won't sweep this series. They're going to they are going to be challenged. And more importantly, because the Spurs have beat them in the regular season, the Spurs are going to be looking at them like, yeah. Y'all, we we we've seen we've been here, done that. We we think we're better. Now, the playoffs are a different game. I'm just telling you, mindset wise, if I'm in the front office, or if I'm on that coaching staff, I'm showing our guys all that film. Hey, this is how we beat them. This is how hey, hey, this game we curb stomped them this game. I need you guys coming out with this type of energy. We respect them, but don't forget you're this. You're the they everybody wants to crown them. Everybody's already talking about what a second championship means for SGA's legacy. They got to go through us first. And that's exactly I like all the highlights and stuff that that where we were beating these guys and getting physical in the regular season. I'm like, yo, let's do that again because in the playoffs they're going to let us get a little bit more physical. Let's lean into that. We have it like, listen, the Spurs have a legitimate chance. Do not be surprised if they win this series. I won't be.
